newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-BOY FAN ALMOST SILENCES PISTOL PETE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BOY FAN ALMOST SILENCES PISTOL PETE.

text.p: At Roland Garros back in 1994 a gawky young boy approached world number one Pete Sampras and asked politely for his autograph.
The next time the two met was on Monday on centre court at the Australian Open and the same young boy showed no respect at all for the decade's greatest male tennis star.
He broke his serve in the opening set and went on to win a tie-break. He fired 20 fast, deep aces. He pushed Sampras all over the court with driving forehands.
Experience won the day, Sampras leaving the sauna-like court a 6-7 6-3 6-4 3-6 6-4 winner, but it was a close-run thing.
"Next time I hope he ask me for autograph," crowed Slovakian teenager Dominik Hrbaty.

Hrbaty, who has just turned 19, has made a remarkable start to his career. Turning professional last year after promising amateur results, he jumped 287 places up the rankings to become the youngest man in the top 100.

His end-year ranking of 77 earned him a place at his debut grand slam, the Australian Open. A five-set win over Australian Sandon Stolle in the first round set fans talking before Sweden's Nicklas Kulti and 16th seed Alberto Berasategui of Spain became the next fall guys.
But few gave Hrbaty a hope before his fourth-round tie with "Pistol Pete" Sampras, the dominant force in men's tennis for the past five years and winner of eight grand slam titles.
Unaware he had signed any autograph in Paris, Sampras said he would not recognise Hrbaty if he bumped into him.
But Hrbaty, already a master of positive thinking, told reporters: "If I play my best tennis, I'll beat him."
And he was right -- Sampras rated himself a lucky winner, wise enough just to hang on in the match and hope that heat and inexperience would see the Slovak off.

"I wasn't thinking all match that 'I'm playing the number one in the world'. I was thinking, 'There is my opponent and I have to beat him'," said Hrbaty in faltering English, a sign of how new he still is on the professional circuit.
"I hope next time we meet, we play each other, I beat him. I will try to play better than today.
"If you are going to play, you have to beat them and you have to think always, you have to think positive that you can beat him. Never, you never have to lose in your mind," he said.
Hrbaty began playing tennis at the age of six and is also a keen skier and mountain biker. At 1.83 metres (six foot), he can generate service speeds of over 200 kph.
Sampras had nothing but praise: "I was really impressed with the way he played, I mean really, I think he's going to be a player to be reckoned with over the years."
"With a little bit more experience he has a good chance of beating me."
